head: claude/r-metric-contamination
title: R-metric contamination: confirm the mechanism, ship a Tier-1 detector, propose the Tier-3 fix
body:
## What this is

An **investigation** into R-metric contamination, plus a **Tier-1 detector** that makes it visible. The underlying fix is **Tier-3 and I did not make it** — it is proposed precisely below, with the exact diff, for the operator.

Everything is marked **OBSERVED** (measured, with its population and locator) or **INFERRED** (a conclusion from named measurements, which is falsifiable and in scope to check).

**Every measurement below shares one locator unless stated otherwise:** live journal copy `/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/data/trade_journal.db` on the trainer VM, mtime `2026-09-02T04:28:35Z`, `max(created_at) 2026-09-02T04:11:21Z` (~17 min behind live). Trader serving sha **`2c7ae605`** (`/api/diag/version`, read 2026-09-02T04:33Z, `restart_pending: false`). Probes are committed and re-runnable at `automation/trainer-diag-requests/r-contamination-probe-20260902{b,c,d}.sh` and `r-detector-live-validation-20260902.sh`; their outputs are in `automation/trainer-diag-results/`.

⚠️ **Context that travels with every dollar figure here:** measured fleet `pnlCoverage` is **0.126** — 87% of this fleet's PnL is not a measurement. Every R conclusion below sits on top of that and is **not firmer than the PnL underneath it**.

---

## 1. The mechanism, confirmed at the writer — **OBSERVED**

`src/runtime/order_monitor.py:1349-1357`, inside `_apply_update`:

```python
for o in applied:
    trade_id = o["leg"].get("id")
    if "sl" in updates:
        trade_sync["stop_loss"] = updates["sl"]
    ...
    db.update_trade(int(trade_id), trade_sync)
```

`trades.stop_loss` therefore holds the **CURRENT** stop, not the initial one. **That write is correct for what it was built for** — `/api/bot/positions` reads `trades.stop_loss` to show the operator where the stop *is*, and before it landed every operator surface showed a stale entry-time level (the fix `_apply_update`'s own comment calls "part 2" of the XRP SL-spam work, 2026-07-22). It is destructive only for R, which is defined against **entry-time** risk. This is not a rogue write to delete; it is one column being asked two incompatible questions.

`order_packages.sl` is **not** a preserved alternative: `_apply_update` writes it too (`db.update_order_package(pkg_id, updates)`, line 1408). **OBSERVED:** of 1325 gradeable rows, `order_packages.sl == trades.stop_loss` on **929**, differs on **36**, and no package joins on **360**. The 36 are the documented asymmetry — the package write is skipped when not every leg amends.

### Is a correct R recoverable for historical rows? **Partly — OBSERVED, and this is the finding that decides whether the fix is forward-only.**

`order_packages.meta` carries the strategy's signal-time **`risk_per_unit`**, written once at package creation (`src/units/strategies/{trend_donchian,htf_pullback_trend_2h,ict_scalp,turtle_soup,squeeze_breakout_4h,fade_breakout_4h,fvg_range_15m,hf_*}.py`). `_apply_update` writes only `sl`/`tp`, so **a trailing amend cannot reach it**.

- **682 of 1346** closed non-backtest rows (50.7%) carry a declared `risk_per_unit`.
- Worked example, trade **4773** (`ict_scalp_mgc_15m`, long): entry `4364.6`, stored stop `4371.1469` (**above** entry), `order_packages.meta.risk_per_unit` **`18.947142857143263`**. Stored distance `6.5469`. The declared risk is **2.89×** the stored one — and on the wrong side.
- **INFERRED:** the fix is therefore **not forward-only**. ~51% of history is backfillable from a record that already exists. The other ~49% — including **all 318 `vwap` real-money rows and all 283 `pairs_*` rows** — has no independent record and is permanently ungradeable, which is why `unverified` must exist as a state rather than being rounded to "clean".

---

## 2. Contamination is **concentrated, not uniform** — OBSERVED

Population: `status='closed' AND pnl IS NOT NULL AND is_backtest=0`, **n = 1346**. ⚠️ This is **WIDER than `/api/bot/performance`'s**, which also drops reconciler / superseded / reset-flat rows — stated so the numbers are not read as that route's.

**Naive wrong-side count: 226 of 1325 gradeable (17.06%)** — which reproduces the handed 17.2% on a 2.8× larger population.

**But 108 of those 226 are a different defect, and the detector separates them (see §4).** After separation:

| state | n | share |
|---|--:|--:|
| `contaminated` (proven not the initial stop) | **118** | 8.8% |
| `confirmed_initial` | 156 | 11.6% |
| `unverified` (**we could not look — NOT clean**) | **1051** | 78.1% |
| `no_basis` (no R to grade) | 21 | 1.6% |

Partition sums to 1346 exactly (asserted in the live-validation run).

### By strategy — the concentration maps onto **which families trail a stop**

| strategy | acct | n | contaminated | % |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `mgc_trend_1h` | paper | 19 | **18** | **94.7%** |
| `ict_scalp_sol_5m` | paper | 29 | 13 | 44.8% |
| `ict_scalp_avax_5m` | paper | 30 | 11 | 36.7% |
| `ict_scalp_5m` | paper | 47 | 9 | 19.1% |
| `ict_scalp_5m` | **real_money** | 33 | 9 | 27.3% |
| `ict_scalp_mgc_15m` | paper | 6 | 4 | 66.7% |
| … | | | | |
| **`vwap`** | **real_money** | **318** | **0** | **0.0%** |
| **`pairs_sol_eth_a/b`, `pairs_bnb_btc_a/b`** | paper | **283** | **0** | **0.0%** |
| all `*_1d` legs | paper | 19 | 0 | 0.0% |

**INFERRED:** the zero-contamination families are exactly the ones with no trailing monitor — `vwap` exits on `vwap_cross`, and the pairs sleeve runs its own isolated executor (`pairs_executor.run_pairs_tick`, not `multi_account_execute`). That the split falls on this line is **independent corroboration of the writer mechanism**, derived from data rather than from the code read.

### By exit path

| exit path | n | contaminated (naive wrong-side) | % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `intent_reduce_executed` | 33 | 33 | 100.0% ← **but see §4: all mirrored-bracket, not trailed** |
| `giveback_stop` | 3 | 3 | 100.0% |
| `tp` | 60 | 19 | 31.7% |
| `netting_attributed` | 38 | 12 | 31.6% |
| `sl_cross` | 107 | 27 | 25.2% |
| `reconciler_filled` | 441 | 107 | 24.3% |
| `sl` | 173 | 13 | 7.5% |
| `vwap_cross` · `pairs_*` · `intent_reduce` · `stale_stop` | 102 · 170 · 38 · 13 | 0 | 0.0% |

---

## 3. Consumer inventory — **and this materially corrects the brief's framing**

The brief says the contamination reaches *"R-based promotion gates"*. **I checked the two automated gates and NEITHER reads R.** That is a real correction, and it lowers the severity from "an automated gate promotes on a number 2 orders of magnitude off" to "every human/Claude review verdict does".

| consumer | what it reads | DECISION or DISPLAY | contaminated? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/bot/performance` — `totalR` / `expectancyR` / `rTradeCount` per headline, strategy, assetClass | `_clean_trades.r_multiple(pnl, entry, **stop_loss**, qty, mult)` | the **publisher** | **YES — origin** |
| **M7 strategy-review packet** `scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py` → `/api/bot/strategies/{name}/review`, `/api/bot/strategy-reviews` — the KILL / DEMOTE_SHADOW / TUNE / HOLD gate | `expectancy = pnl_total / n_closed` (**DOLLARS**), `win_rate`, `n_closed` vs `MIN_CLOSED_FOR_ACTION` | **DECISION** | **NO** — verified at `:587-589`, `:721-723`, `:983-984`, `:1030-1071`; the whole action matrix keys on `win`/`exp`/`n` and none is R |
| **R4 research→results gate** `src/runtime/research_results_gate.py::source_verdict` ← `scripts/research/research_results_gate_report.py` | `trades`, `pnlCoverage`, `totalPnlMeasured` | **DECISION** | **NO** — zero `totalR`/`expectancyR`/`stop_loss` references in the module |
| `src/runtime/net_r_label.py::risk_usd_for_trade` → `net_r_for_trade` | `trade["stop_loss"]` **directly** | label producer | **YES — a SECOND, INDEPENDENT site** |
| `net-r-regrade` system-action (Tier-1) → `scripts/research/net_r_regrade.py` | `net_r_for_trade`; emits the **sign-flip flag**, documented as *"a Tier-3 review candidate"* | **DECISION-FEEDING** | **YES** (inherits) |
| `scripts/research/component_edge_report.py` | `t.stop_loss` (`:265`) via its **own duplicate copy** of `r_multiple` (`:152`) | research evidence | **YES**, DB-cohort path |
| `/system-review` · `/performance-review` · `comms/reports/*` | `expectancyR` / `totalR` as review evidence | **DECISION (human/Claude judgment)** — *this is where it actually bites* | **YES** |
| `ROADMAP.md:243` · `docs/research/M27-GLD-1H-PROMOTION-PACKET-2026-08-14.md:59` · `docs/claude/WORKPLAN-2026-08-21.md:330` | quoted `expectancyR` figures already written down as evidence | **DECISION evidence, already committed** | **YES** |
| Svelte SPA | `totalR` / `expectancyR` | **display** | YES, display-only |

**Two things worth flagging separately:**
- `net_r_label.py` is an **independent second site**, not a downstream of `/performance`. Fixing `r_multiple` alone would leave it contaminated.
- `component_edge_report.py:152` carries a **duplicate of the `r_multiple` formula**. Two copies of a risk denominator is how the fix half-lands.

---

## 4. The detector (Tier-1, shipped here)

**`src/runtime/r_provenance.py`** — pure, no I/O, the direct sibling of `src/runtime/provenance.py` one derivative up: that grades the R **numerator** (`pnl`), this grades the **denominator**.

**Four states, never collapsed**, and `unverified` is the one that matters:

| state | meaning |
|---|---|
| `contaminated` | **PROVEN** not the initial stop. Sole proof, threshold-free: the stop sits on the **wrong side of entry** — not a risk level, a locked-in profit. |
| `confirmed_initial` | Correct side **AND** distance matches the independent signal-time `risk_per_unit`. Both halves required. |
| `unverified` | **We could not look.** Side-plausible, and either no declared record or one that disagrees. ⚠️ **NOT "clean"** — a stop trailed to just *short* of entry is side-plausible and equally wrong. 78.1% of the population. |
| `no_basis` | No R to grade (missing inputs / non-positive risk) — the rows `r_multiple` already returns `None` for. Emitted so the four **sum to the population by construction**. |

### The failed cross-check, and what it forced — OBSERVED

I built the second axis, then ran my own cross-check: *rows that are `confirmed_initial` on distance AND wrong-side on sign should be ~0.* **It came back 34.** Rather than pick an explanation, I probed it:

- **All 34 are `setup_type='intent_reduce'`**, and `trades.direction` is the **opposite** of `order_packages.direction` on every one (108 rows disagree that way overall).
- **34 of 34 have an incoherent `entry`/`sl`/`tp` ordering** — the *whole bracket* is inverted, not just the stop.
- **INFERRED:** this is correct by design. A reduce leg's `direction` is the *closing* side while its SL/TP are inherited from the *original* position. The **side test's input** is unreliable there — it is not evidence of a trail.

The discriminator is proof-grade and needs no threshold: **a trail moves the STOP; a mirror moves BOTH.** A row whose take-profit is *also* on the wrong side is graded `unverified` / `bracket_mirrored_vs_direction`.

**Live validation of the shipped module** (`r-detector-live-validation-20260902`, module sha256 `fd40d801c4a3…` fetched from this branch's raw URL so the code under test *is* the code that ran): **108 of 108** mirrored-bracket rows are `intent_reduce`, and **no other `setup_type` appears**. The discriminator isolates exactly the known-cause population and nothing else. It moves `htf_pullback_trend_2h` paper from 25 "wrong-side" to **0 contaminated / 48 unverified**, and the fleet from 226 to **118**.

⚠️ **`/api/bot/performance` does NOT apply `exclude_intent_reduce_predicate`** (only reconciler / superseded / reset-flat), so these rows *are* inside the R population. Reported, not fixed here — it is a separate call.

### The second axis is published as a NUMBER, not a verdict — and here is why

The ratio `declared_initial_risk / stored_stop_distance` (>1 = the trail signature). **STATE THE POPULATION — the two side-populations have completely different distributions and pooling them (which my own first pass did) describes neither:**

| population | n | median | p75 | p90 | p95 | max | ≥2.0 | **<0.99** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **correct-side** | 456 | **1.0000** | 1.0262 | 1.1411 | 1.3370 | 211.7 | 12 (2.6%) | **111 (24.3%)** |
| **wrong-side** | 226 | 1.0353 | **5.3117** | 17.95 | 62.60 | **3014.2** | 91 (40.3%) | 37 |

**INFERRED:** the dense mass at ~1.0 on correct-side rows is **not a trail** — 24.3% of it reads *below* 0.99 (stored stop **wider** than declared), which trailing cannot produce. It is two-sided basis/rounding noise whose cause I did **not** establish. So a distance disagreement is **never** graded `contaminated`; it lands in `unverified`, and the bar-crossing count is published beside the states with its own denominator (`tightenedVsDeclared` / `declaredRiskRecords` / `ratioBar`). **12 correct-side rows cross 2.0 — those are the ones the side proof cannot see**, which is the entire reason the axis is published at all.

That the two populations separate this cleanly is **independent corroboration that the side test discriminates rather than merely fires**.

### Where it is published

`/api/bot/performance` gains an `rProvenance` block on the **headline**, on **each `perStrategy` row**, and on the **empty/errored envelope** (explicit zeros — a key that vanishes makes a consumer branch on absence, and absence is not a state). It rides into the `paper` / `paperPortfolio` sub-blocks for free.

⚠️ **NOTHING IS EXCLUDED FROM ANY AGGREGATE.** `totalR`, `expectancyR`, `rTradeCount` and `rCoverage` are byte-identical — asserted by `test_totalR_and_rCoverage_are_UNCHANGED_by_the_detector`. Dropping the rows would convert a visible-wrong number into an invisible-wrong one over an unstated population.

### Both-direction controls — the verification bar

**67 new tests**, and every discrimination is asserted in **both** directions, because a classifier returning `contaminated` unconditionally would pass a one-sided suite:

| control | positive | negative |
|---|---|---|
| long trailed past entry | fires | same row, stop at 99 → does not |
| short trailed past entry | fires | same row, stop at 101 → does not |
| the live worst case (trade 5027, R=+3672.32) | fires | — |
| mirrored bracket (trade 3319) | **does not** fire | same row, TP moved back → **does** |
| declared risk matches | `confirmed_initial` | declared risk disagrees → `unverified`, **never** `contaminated` |
| the side test's blind spot (stop trailed to 99.99) | side test **misses** it, asserted | the ratio axis **catches** it, asserted |
| a legacy schema with no `direction` | degrades to `unverified` | **never** to `confirmed_initial` |

**Mutation-verified**, not assumed: hard-coding `"noBasis": 0` in the route makes `test_the_four_states_partition_the_population` **fail**; restoring it passes.

⚠️ **Honest limit on the `collapsed-state-guard` registration** (`r_provenance.r_state`, contract #26, passes non-grandfathered): I mutation-tested it and the guard **still reads clean** when the route stops branching on `R_NO_BASIS`, because its consumer evidence is satisfied by any repo file naming the constants — this PR's own test module included. So the guard proves the *contract*, not that the **route** branches on all four. The test above is what actually enforces that, and it is why the partition test now asserts every bucket **non-zero** rather than only that they sum.

---

## 5. The Tier-3 change I propose — **and an explicit statement that I did not make it**

**I did not make this change. No file under `src/units/db/`, `src/units/accounts/`, `src/web/api/_clean_trades.py`, `src/runtime/net_r_label.py` or `src/runtime/order_monitor.py` is touched by this PR.** It is Tier-3 because step 4 changes what a promotion-adjacent number reads and step 5 writes the money DB.

**Rejected first, so it is not re-proposed:** *stop the `_apply_update` mirror.* That re-breaks `/api/bot/positions` — the mirror exists precisely because every operator surface used to show a stale entry-time level. The defect is one column answering two questions, so the fix is to **split the column**, not to delete the write.

**The sequence matters** — shipping step 4 before 1–3 and 5 would make historical R *change* without any of it becoming correct.

1. **`src/units/db/database.py`** — add `initial_stop_loss REAL` to the `trades` DDL, plus an idempotent `_migrate_add_initial_stop_loss(cursor)` alongside the existing `_migrate_add_*` siblings.
2. **`src/units/accounts/execute.py::_log_trade_to_journal`** — set `initial_stop_loss` to the same value it already writes to `stop_loss`, at insert.
3. **`src/units/db/database.py::update_trade`** — **refuse** a write to `initial_stop_loss` on a row that already carries one. Write-once, copying `terminal_state`'s never-overwrite rule verbatim: the first observation is the honest one.
4. **`src/web/api/_clean_trades.py::r_multiple`** — take the risk basis from `initial_stop_loss` when present, else `order_packages.meta.risk_per_unit`, else fall back to `stop_loss` **with the row graded `unverified`** by this PR's module. Then point `src/runtime/net_r_label.py::risk_usd_for_trade` and `scripts/research/component_edge_report.py:152` at the same resolver — **one owner for the risk denominator, or the fix half-lands** (there are three copies of the formula today).
5. **New `scripts/ops/backfill_initial_stop_loss.py`** (**Tier-2** — a money-DB write) — one-shot, `initial_stop_loss = entry ∓ meta.risk_per_unit`, sign taken from `order_packages.direction` (**not** `trades.direction`, per §4). Covers **682 of 1346** rows; the rest stay `NULL` and grade `unverified`, which is the honest outcome and must not be papered over with a `stop_loss` copy.

**What I would ask the operator to decide, specifically:** whether the fallback in step 4 keeps using `stop_loss` (R stays computable for 100% of rows, ~78% of it flagged `unverified`) or returns `None` (R becomes honest-but-thin — `rCoverage` would drop toward the confirmed+backfilled fraction). This PR takes no position; it makes the choice legible either way.

---

## 6. What I did NOT do

- Did **not** touch `config/`, `ROADMAP.md`, `docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json`, any `*-review-backlog.json`, the order path, or `order_monitor.py`.
- Did **not** exclude any row from any aggregate.
- Did **not** establish the cause of the near-1.0 ratio mass on correct-side rows. It is reported as unexplained.
- Did **not** resolve whether the 3 `giveback_stop` rows at 100% wrong-side are the same mechanism (n=3; too thin to call).

### Backlog rows I would file (text here, per scope — the files are owned by a live drain)

- **`BL-20260902-TRADES-STOP-LOSS-HOLDS-THE-TRAILED-STOP-SO-R-IS-COMPUTED-FROM-A-RISK-THE-TRADE-NEVER-TOOK`** — severity `high`, tier `3`. `order_monitor._apply_update:1349-1357` mirrors every confirmed trailing amend onto `trades.stop_loss`, and `_clean_trades.r_multiple` derives the R denominator from it. Measured 2026-09-02 (n=1346, journal copy mtime 2026-09-02T04:28:35Z, trader sha 2c7ae605): 118 rows proven contaminated, 1051 unverifiable, worst leg `mgc_trend_1h` paper at 18 of 19; worst single row R = **+3672.32** (trade 5027, stop distance 0.000885 on a ~$100 instrument). Detector shipped (`src/runtime/r_provenance.py`); the fix is the 5-step Tier-3 proposal in PR §5. **`resolution_criteria`:** `trades.initial_stop_loss` exists, is write-once, is backfilled for the 682 rows with a declared `risk_per_unit`, and `/api/bot/performance` reports `rProvenance.contaminated == 0` for every row whose R is computed from it.
- **`BL-20260902-THREE-INDEPENDENT-COPIES-OF-THE-R-RISK-DENOMINATOR-FORMULA`** — severity `medium`, tier `1`. `_clean_trades.r_multiple`, `net_r_label.risk_usd_for_trade` and `component_edge_report.py:152` each implement `|entry − stop| × qty × multiplier` separately, so the Tier-3 fix above must be applied three times or it half-lands. **`resolution_criteria`:** one owner; the other two import it; a guard or test asserts no fourth copy.
- **`BL-20260902-PERFORMANCE-DOES-NOT-EXCLUDE-INTENT-REDUCE-ROWS`** — severity `medium`, tier `1`. `/api/bot/performance` applies the reconciler / superseded / reset-flat exclusions but not `exclude_intent_reduce_predicate`, so 108 direction-mirrored reduce legs sit inside the R and PnL populations. Whether they *should* be excluded is a call I did not make. **`resolution_criteria`:** an explicit decision recorded either way, and the predicate applied or a comment saying why not.

---

## FOR THE MANAGER

- **DRAFT. Do not merge without the Tier-1/Tier-3 split being read** — §4 is Tier-1 and shippable on its own; §5 is a proposal for the operator and **is not in this diff**.
- **Guards:** `PASS 51 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 19`, run **after** the final commit (`824254e9`), and **CI `guards` is green on that head too**. Three failed on the first pass and all three are fixed in-branch: `ruff` E702, a dangling `BL-20260722-XRP-SLSPAM` reference (removed rather than filed, since the backlog files are out of scope for me), and `layer-guard` exiting 127 on a missing `lint-imports` binary (passes once installed: 6 kept, 0 broken).
- **Tests:** 67 new, 103 in the targeted suite, all green locally. **CI `pytest-run` is GREEN on this head (`824254e9`)** — the full suite in the correct dependency environment, which is the authority and settles it.
- **A correction I owe you, because an earlier draft of this bullet over-claimed.** It read *"I verified this is not my change: `origin/main` produces the identical 99 errors"*. What I had actually verified was narrower — the 99 **collection** errors, which are identical on `main`. A later full-suite comparison came back **983 failed / 11,592 passed / 163 errors** on `main` against **999 / 11,863 / 172** on the branch, and I could not attribute the delta: that baseline ran in a **different working directory** from a `--shared` clone (no untracked `runtime_logs/`, no `.env`, different path resolution), and the `+271 passed` against 67 new tests is the tell that the two runs were not comparable. Re-run apples-to-apples in the **same** working directory: `main` **994 / 11,801 / 172** vs branch **999 / 11,863 / 172** — **errors identical**, and the same ref swung 983→994 failures between two runs, so this sandbox is not a stable instrument. **CI green on the full suite is what actually answers the question**, and it does.
- **The brief's premise needed correcting and I have corrected it in §3:** neither automated gate (M7 packet, R4 results gate) reads R. The contamination reaches decisions through review sessions and promotion packets a human reads — real, but a different severity than stated. Please carry that correction rather than the original framing.
- **Nothing was messaged to the operator.** §5 is the Tier-3 item that needs their yes/no, and §5's last paragraph names the one question I would put to them.
